chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Qasim ibn Yahya from his grandfather al-Hasan ibn Rashid from Ya'qub ibn Ja'far who said:
I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'Upon each nostril of the beasts is a shaytan. So when any one of you wishes to bridle it, let him mention the name of Allah, Exalted and Glorious.'

key_terms.شَيْطَانٌ: Shaytan (devil/demon), referring to the spiritual influence or instinct within the animal
key_terms.لْيُسَمِّ اللَّهَ: Let him mention the name of Allah (invoking Allah's name)
key_terms.يُلْجِمَهَا: To bridle or put a halter on an animal

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended practice when bridling an animal according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), linking the physical act of bridling animals to the spiritual concept of *shaytan* residing in each nostril, a view reflecting the Shi'a understanding of unseen forces influencing animal behavior. This ruling emphasizes that invoking Allah's name (*tasmiyah*) during the process serves not only as a legal requirement for control but also as a spiritual safeguard against these subtle influences. The practice underscores the integration of daily agricultural or travel activities with continuous remembrance of God, a hallmark of Shi'a jurisprudence.
